chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, on the authority of Jamil, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

There are two matters; whichever comes first terminates the waiting period of the divorced woman who has irregular menstruation (mustarabah al-haid). If three white months pass for her during which no blood is seen, she is divorced by them. And if three menstruations pass for her, with no three months between each menstruation, she is divorced by the menstruation.

key_terms.أَشْهُرٍ بِيضٍ: White months (months of cleanliness without menstruation)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَرَابَةُ: A woman with irregular or uncertain menstruation

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period determined for a divorced woman with irregular menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal details the juristic criteria for determining the end of the waiting period (iddah) for a divorced woman with irregular menstruation (mustarabah al-haid), distinguishing between three consecutive months of cleanliness and three distinct menstruations. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise temporal intervals to resolve legal uncertainty, ensuring the woman's status is clearly defined before remarriage. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions regarding iddah in cases where biological signs are ambiguous.
